title: Four scams aimed at UPI users, and how to see through them
summary: Fraudsters in India use UPI, KYC warnings and fake officials to rush you. Knowing what real messages look like is the best protection for you and your family.

sections.heading: Your UPI PIN only ever sends money
sections.body: A 'buyer' sends a UPI collect request and asks you to enter your PIN to receive payment. You never need a PIN to receive money; entering it sends money out of your account.

sections.heading: Urgency is the scammer's main tool
sections.body: An SMS says your account will be blocked today unless you update your KYC through a link. Banks ask you to use the branch or the official app. A video call from a 'CBI officer' claiming a 'digital arrest' is always fake: it does not exist in Indian law, and police never ask you to transfer money. Report it at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.

sections.heading: If you must pay to earn, walk away
sections.body: WhatsApp 'jobs' that pay ₹5,000 a day for liking videos start by asking for a small registration fee, then ask for bigger deposits. Real jobs never charge you to start.

sections.heading: What real messages look like
sections.body: A debit alert for a payment you made, with no link, is normal. An OTP you requested yourself is real too, and the bank's message warns you never to share it with anyone, including bank staff.

example.title: The call Ananya's father got
example.body: Ananya's father receives a video call from a man in uniform saying a parcel with drugs was booked on his Aadhaar and he is under 'digital arrest'. Because Ananya had explained this scam at dinner, he hangs up, calls her, and they report it together on 1930. No money leaves his account.

takeaway: Never enter your UPI PIN or share an OTP because someone asked: hang up, check for yourself, and report on 1930.

quiz.question: A buyer sends a UPI request and asks you to enter your PIN to receive ₹4,999. What do you do?
options: Decline: a PIN only ever sends money
Ask them to send it again
quiz.why: You never need your UPI PIN to receive money. Entering it sends money out.

quiz.question: A 'CBI officer' on a video call says you're under digital arrest. What's true?
options: You must transfer money to prove innocence
Digital arrest doesn't exist; hang up and report on 1930
Stay on the call until it's resolved
quiz.why: Police never ask you to transfer money. Report it at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.

quiz.question: Which message is normal?
options: 'Your account will be blocked today, update KYC at this link'
'₹250 debited for your Swiggy order via UPI', with no link
quiz.why: A debit alert for a payment you made, with no link or request, is a normal bank message.
